findings.reason: The protected implementation is concise, conventional, and expert-interview ready. `remove_start`, `remove_end`, `start`, `end`, and `answer` expose the complete interval-classification state; the disjoint fast path and two strict residual tests mirror the half-open contract directly; and no helper, hidden mutation, or clever compression obscures the sweep. No material clarity, correctness, or complexity improvement warrants a candidate.

For an input interval [start,end), `end <= remove_start` or `start >= remove_end` proves empty intersection under half-open semantics, so copying the interval is exact. Otherwise, `start < remove_start` emits precisely the surviving left portion and `end > remove_end` emits precisely the surviving right portion; strict comparisons exclude empty pieces. These pieces partition the input interval outside the removal range, and source order plus left-before-right emission preserves sorted disjoint output.

An independent oracle explicitly formed the intersection [max(start,remove_start), min(end,remove_end)) and retained the portions on either side. It, the protected app source, the immutable native source, and a separate front-insertion control agreed on all ten visible cases, all three benchmark tiers, 6,300 exhaustive small databases, 10,000 deterministic random databases, and a legal 10,000-interval maximum-cardinality database. Inputs remained unchanged.

The exhaustive corpus used every nonempty sorted disjoint list of up to three intervals over endpoints -3 through 3 against every removal interval over -4 through 4. The seeded random corpus exercised 212,047 no-overlap intervals, 85,924 complete removals, 4,564 left residuals, 3,461 right residuals, 117 true splits, and 1,476 exact endpoint touches. Separate checks covered both coordinate limits and n = 10^4.

The hidden legal tiers remain unchanged at n = 512, 2,048, and 8,192, a 16x span, and retain every interval so output construction governs scaling. Across three real-test runs, the protected source passed at extra-growth exponents -0.05 through +0.00 and an independent linear control passed at +0.04 through +0.05. The originally documented front-insertion comparator was unreliable at Python's optimized native-list-shift constants, passing two of three runs at the 0.15 threshold. The note now names a correct repeated-concatenation control instead; that O(n^2) implementation returned every correct output and failed only scaling in five of five runs at +0.42 through +0.44. No tier input, size, expected output, or hidden flag changed.

All three authenticated source examples remain first and exact. Three hidden real rows were converted to visible trials without changing their inputs or expected outputs, and a visible coordinate-limit split was added. All ten ordinary fixtures are now visible samples or trials and cover no overlap on both sides, exact endpoint touching, complete coverage, exact removal, left trim, right trim, a true split, several overlaps, gaps, negative coordinates, and both -10^9 and 10^9.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1272, Python as the app language, and Solution.removeInterval as the verified native entrypoint. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms sorted disjoint half-open input intervals, membership a <= x < b, set subtraction by toBeRemoved, sorted disjoint output, interval count from 1 through 10^4, and endpoint bounds from -10^9 through 10^9 with a_i < b_i.

The protected app and immutable Accepted native sources have identical endpoint unpacking, interval traversal, non-overlap predicate, left and right residual tests, emission order, and return value; their only structural difference is the required app function versus LeetCode class-method wrapper and native typing import. submission.json remains bound to verified submission 2068263023, and both sources and the manifest remain unchanged.

The complete Approach matches the protected implementation exactly. It derives all four interval outcomes, explains why the non-strict no-overlap and strict residual comparisons implement half-open boundaries, proves set-difference correctness and output ordering, gives exact O(n) time and O(n) output-space bounds with O(1) auxiliary state, and discusses meaningful alternatives and every material edge case.

The modular Reference preserves the real-number set model, half-open membership relation, sorted disjoint input and output requirements, subtraction semantics, all three source examples in order, both constraints, and both source hints without adding an unsupported constraint for toBeRemoved.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed three examples without explanations, two constraints, two hints, and no source tables, images, diagrams, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds all five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 7bfa7b4e633ea3efb4588a5875041edffe7cbdcaef576dd6f06197509d9bef7d and validates without errors.

coverage: The first three visible samples preserve all authenticated source examples in exact order, including every interval, removal endpoint, and output interval.

Ten visible ordinary fixtures cover minimum cardinality, both coordinate limits, disjoint removals on either side, exact half-open touching, exact and complete removal, left and right trims, a true split, multiple overlaps, gaps, and negative-to-positive coordinates.

The protected and immutable native sources matched two independent controls on every fixed input, 6,300 exhaustive small databases, 10,000 seeded random databases, and a maximum-cardinality 10,000-interval database.

The three hidden performance-only tiers retain n = 512, 2,048, and 8,192 intervals. Repeated real tests accept protected and independent linear controls, while a correct repeated-concatenation control passes every output and consistently fails only scaling.
